classification.difficultyReason: Infer the overlapping region from two sport totals and a known union, then distinguish both, exclusive regions and exactly one.

content.prompt:
Use an appropriate Venn diagram.

In a group of 40 students, 26 play tennis and 19 play soccer. Assuming that each of the 40 students plays at least one of these sports, find the probability that a student chosen at random from this group:

answer.worked:
Let $T$ denote tennis and $S$ soccer. Since every student plays at least one sport, the union contains 40 students.

$$\begin{align*}n(T\cap S)&=26+19-40\\n(T\cap S)&=5\\P(T\cap S)&=\frac{5}{40}\\P(T\cap S)&=\frac18\end{align*}$$

The tennis-only region contains $26-5=21$ students and the soccer-only region contains $19-5=14$ students.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{exactly one sport})&=\frac{21+14}{40}\\P(\text{exactly one sport})&=\frac{35}{40}\\P(\text{exactly one sport})&=\frac78\end{align*}$$
